client_alerts.headline: Microsoft 365 MC1472007 takes effect today (Oct 25)
client_alerts.body: Advanced Copilot agent and plugin uploads **stay open to all users by default** unless a tenant admin restricts them. Clients who have not reviewed their Copilot agent-upload policy should do so now: an unreviewed default means any user can publish an agent that touches tenant data.

client_alerts.headline: Node2Shell: patch Node.js estates (fixed Oct 21)
client_alerts.body: A Brotli-decoder flaw in Node.js, found by OpenAI's Codex Security researchers, follows last week's PHP2Shell scramble. Ask clients with Node.js services (including vendor appliances and SaaS integrations) for confirmation that the Oct 21 patch is deployed. **AI-found bugs are shrinking the patch window**, so DR runbooks should assume faster exploitation.

top_moves.title: Node2Shell: AI-found Node.js flaw extends "Black October" to a second runtime
top_moves.body: OpenAI Codex Security reported a Brotli-decoder flaw in Node.js; patches shipped Oct 21. Coming days after PHP2Shell, it confirms AI-assisted bug hunting is now producing **high-impact runtime vulnerabilities on a weekly cadence**.

top_moves.title: Replit moves most of its AI spend from Anthropic to OpenAI ($100M+/yr)
top_moves.body: The Information reports one of Anthropic's largest coding customers is shifting the bulk of its model spend to OpenAI. A live example of **AI vendor concentration risk**: platforms your clients depend on can swap the model underneath them without notice.

top_moves.title: Coding agents get computer control and auto-review
top_moves.body: GitHub put Computer Use in Copilot CLI and desktop into public preview, Cursor 3.24 added auto-review safety controls, and OpenAI pushed GPT-6.1 Sol to paid Codex plans (single-source report). Agents that drive desktops widen the blast radius that change-control must cover.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: Codex Security researchers found the Node2Shell Node.js flaw, and GPT-6.1 Sol reportedly reached paid Codex plans.
providers.detail: OpenAI's security research arm is now a visible source of critical CVEs (Node2Shell, patched Oct 21). GPT-6.1 Sol is reported on paid Codex plans, and Replit is moving $100M+/yr of spend to OpenAI. A single newsletter claims OpenAI paused frontier training after a containment incident; this is **unverified** and not reported elsewhere.
providers.alertReason: AI-found Node.js vulnerability requires patch confirmation

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Replit shifts most of its AI spend to OpenAI, a $100M+/yr customer loss ahead of the IPO.
providers.detail: The Information reports Replit moved most model spend from Anthropic to OpenAI. Claude Code reportedly reached build 2.1.295. No public S-1 yet; the confidential filing dates from June 1.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: No new release; the consumer tier changes continue (Free on Flash-Lite since Oct 9, Plus losing Pro on emailed dates).
providers.detail: An aggregator lists a 'Gemini 4 Argon' release on Oct 1 with no primary Google source. Sundar Pichai said Google is far from the end state of recursive self-improvement. Check which Gemini tier client staff are actually on before relying on Pro-level output.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Quiet since Grok Voice 3.0 (Oct 14); Grok 5 is still not shipped, with the Oct 31 prediction market open.
providers.detail: Grok 4.7 (Sept 21) remains the flagship and is on Amazon Bedrock. An experimental TypeScript SDK shipped Oct 2. Musk's 'two to three months' GPT-6-class claim from late September is unconfirmed.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: No new release; Meta's frontier models remain closed and API-only, with no new open Llama.
providers.detail: Muse Spark (April 2026) replaced Llama in Meta's products and Llama 4 is still the latest open release. Clients planning on self-hosted Llama for data control should not count on a new open-weight version.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: No new release; the Large 4 preview (Oct 6) is still API-only, with open weights to come.
providers.detail: Mistral remains the main EU-hosted option for data-residency-sensitive clients. An unverified roundup mentions a 'Le Chonk 1T' model; no official changelog entry.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: No dated October release; publisher litigation (at least seven suits) is the story.
providers.detail: Model Council and Perplexity Computer remain the differentiators for multi-model cross-checking. The litigation backlog is worth a line in vendor risk notes if clients use it for research deliverables.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: MC1472007 takes effect today: advanced agent and plugin uploads stay open to all users by default.
providers.detail: The October roadmap adds local inferencing, actionable federated connectors and Teams/Entra ID backup enhancements. Copilot in classic Outlook finishes GCC/GCC High/DoD rollout this month. Tenant admins should review agent-upload policy today.
providers.alertReason: Default-open agent uploads take effect Oct 25

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: Computer Use enters public preview in Copilot CLI and the desktop apps.
providers.detail: Copilot agents can now operate a desktop, not just a repo (single-source report). Usage-based billing since June 1 and share pressure from Cursor and Claude Code (both 18% vs Copilot 29%) remain the backdrop.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: Cursor 3.24 ships auto-review safety controls for agent changes.
providers.detail: Builds on September's Rollouts and Security Review bots. Auto-review is the kind of control BCP/DR change-management reviews should ask development teams about.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: No release found; the long quiet stretch continues.
providers.detail: Still the fastest prompt-to-deck tool; ChatGPT Slides (Oct 16) is now a direct competitor for Pro/Business users.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new release; Notion Workers billing against credits (from Oct 15) is the last change.
providers.detail: Watch credit consumption if Notion Workers are running scheduled automations for client workspaces.

month_themes.then: Agent data-access incidents (OpenAI Medicare files), API deprecations (Sora removed), coding-tool deployment bots (Cursor Rollouts)
month_themes.now: AI-found runtime vulnerabilities (PHP2Shell, Node2Shell), AI vendor concentration and switching (Replit), coding agents gaining desktop control

habits.shift: Add a 'compressed patch window' assumption: AI-found flaws like PHP2Shell and Node2Shell are being exploited within days, so recovery runbooks should not assume a 30-day patch cycle.
Map NIST SP 1353 (GenAI in CSF 2.0, comments closed Oct 15) into control summaries; it requires a qualified human reviewer for AI-generated mappings, which matches how you already work.

habits.tool: Perplexity Model Council or ChatGPT GPT-6 Sol
habits.shift: Ask every SaaS vendor which model provider sits underneath and how they'd tell you if it changed. Replit's switch shows the swap happens silently.
No change. Consider an optional 'AI supply-chain review' line item for third-party AI agents and model dependencies.
ChatGPT Slides (Oct 16) now lets teams keep editing a deck in a shared Space. Try it for one internal deck before switching client work away from Gamma.
No change. ChatGPT audio uploads (Oct 6) can turn a recorded tabletop debrief into a transcript and summary.

habits.task: Client advisory on AI data risk
habits.tool: M365 admin center + Claude for drafting
habits.shift: Make today's MC1472007 default (open agent uploads) the opener for any M365 client check-in this week.

community.signal: GLM-5.2 is the most-discussed thread topic, alongside Unsloth's Gemma 4 QAT release and a push for open coding-session datasets.
community.so_what: Strong open-weight options keep improving; relevant for clients who need on-prem AI for data-residency reasons.

community.signal: A highly upvoted post (~670) debates a Musk tweet on whether current GPT models exceed the smartest humans; another measures weekly limits on the $100 Pro Lite plan.
community.so_what: Usage limits vary between users and may be A/B tested, so don't promise clients a fixed ChatGPT throughput.

community.signal: No verifiable top posts for this week surfaced; the performance-and-bugs megathread remains the hub for outage reports.
community.so_what: Use status.claude.com, not Reddit, as the source of truth for Claude availability in client continuity plans.

watch.title: Grok 5 by Oct 31?
watch.body: A prediction market on a general-public Grok 5 release by Oct 31 is still open; nothing official yet.

watch.title: More AI-found runtime flaws
watch.body: After PHP2Shell and Node2Shell, expect further AI-discovered CVEs in common runtimes. Confirm client patch SLAs can handle a weekly cadence.

watch.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro open weights (due Nov 4)
watch.body: Moonshot promised open weights by Nov 4; another strong open model for on-prem use if it ships.

watch.title: Unverified: OpenAI frontier-training pause
watch.body: One newsletter claims OpenAI took frontier training offline after a containment incident. No corroboration found; check before citing to clients.

watch.title: AI cloud capacity sold out for 2026
watch.body: Andy Jassy says AWS AI capacity is sold out for the year. Clients planning DR failover onto GPU capacity should confirm reservations exist.
